description: Make a square bundle photo from clear images of items in your set. Compare each object with the kit, then list exact contents in your product description.
h1: Product Bundle Photos for Items Sold Together
lead: Lay out every item in your kit, take one clear photo, and turn it into a bundle photo in one square scene. Review each object against your actual kit and list the exact contents in your product description. List the included pieces before you start so the arrangement can keep every item visible and your final contents statement stays accurate.
intro: The example shows a skincare set on a round stone tray: a frosted serum bottle with a dropper, a cream jar with a gold lid, and the leaf-printed carton they come in. A folded towel and a few white blossoms set the mood without hiding any piece.

Bundle listings raise one question above all: what do I actually get? One photo with every item, and nothing extra, answers it at a glance. Add it right after your main image on Amazon or Shopify, and use it for gift sets, starter kits, and refill packs.
tip: Upload every piece that comes in the set, box included, and list them in your description, so the photo shows your kit and no extra products.

faq.q: Why did an extra item show up in my bundle photo?
faq.a: That usually happens when a piece is missing from your upload or the description leaves room for guessing. Upload every item, state the exact count, and run it again. Include every item that ships in the source photo and keep each piece visible; a missing accessory can make the bundle promise inaccurate.

faq.q: Can I add the bundle price to the photo?
faq.a: Put the price and any savings line on later, using Canva or a similar app. Text generated inside the image can come out with typos, so the photo is made without it. A top-down reveal works for counted sets, while a review or demo works when shoppers also need to see how the pieces are used.

faq.q: Can the photo show results like glowing skin?
faq.a: Keep the photo about the products themselves. Showing the set is fine, but results such as clearer or younger-looking skin shouldn't be promised in the image or the listing text. Put the finished image beside the contents list and item count on the product page, then compare it with the packed kit before publishing.

faq.q: How should I photograph a multi-piece set?
faq.a: Lay every piece together in one clear photo with even light, so the generated image keeps the correct items and count. Add counts, sizes, and names as editable text in your listing or editor so the information can be corrected without replacing the image.

faq.q: Can I show the bundle on a white background?
faq.a: Yes. Ask for a plain background when the photo is for a listing, or a bright table for a lifestyle shot.  If an item ships in multiple colors or sizes, list each option separately and do not imply that every variation appears in one box image.

faq.q: How many credits does a bundle photo cost?
faq.a: Each bundle photo costs 24 credits. You see the charge before running it, and failed jobs are refunded.  Check the source against the packed kit after generation; the photo can show arrangement, but the seller remains responsible for the exact contents statement.

overview.h2: Answer the Bundle Question in One Frame
overview.p: A bundle image is useful when the shopper can count the pieces without opening a dropdown or reading a long description. Lay out the products, packaging, and any included accessory as one clear group, while keeping decorative props quiet and separate.

overview.h2: Treat the Contents List as the Source of Truth
overview.p: The picture helps people understand the set at a glance; your written contents list still defines what ships. Build the source around the exact inventory so a refill pouch, spare lid, or gift box does not disappear from the composition.

visual.overview: A what’s-in-the-box photo shows what ships as one set. Arrange every item so shoppers can count the pieces, recognize their sizes, and see the packaging they will receive. Keep the products fully visible and use one viewpoint rather than hiding smaller pieces behind the largest object. A skincare starter kit can show its cleanser, serum, and cream together; a canvas travel pouch kit can show the pouch and its accessories. Add item names and quantities in editable listing text after checking the physical package. Leave a gap between pieces so shoppers can count them quickly, and keep the box or pouch recognizable when packaging is part of the offer. This is a contents check, not a promise of extras.
